sections.html:
Russell County is the easternmost county in Alabama, on the Georgia line across the Chattahoochee River from Columbus. Phenix City is the county seat and largest city, and the county forms part of the Columbus, Georgia and Alabama metropolitan area.

It covers 647 square miles, with 641 of land and 6.1 of water. Lee County lies to the north, and Barbour, Bullock and Macon counties touch it inside Alabama. Muscogee, Chattahoochee and Stewart counties in Georgia sit across the state line.

The land is Gulf Coastal Plain with a few rolling hills near the fall line.

sections.h2: How did Russell County get its start, and why is the county seat in Phenix City?
sections.html:
The legislature formed the county in 1832 from land ceded by the Creek, and named it for Colonel Gilbert C. Russell. The seat has moved several times, from Girard in 1833 to Crawford in 1839, then to Seale in 1868, and finally to Phenix City in 1935.

Girard later merged into Phenix City, in 1923. The old seats still have names on the map: Crawford and Seale are unincorporated communities today, and both are outside Phenix City.

Phenix City had a hard stretch in the 1940s and 1950s, when organized crime and corruption took hold. After the 1954 killing of Albert Patterson, who had won the Democratic nomination for state attorney general on a clean-up platform, Governor Gordon Persons declared martial law on July 22, 1954. Civilian control returned on January 17, 1955.

sections.h2: How does the Georgia line shape Russell County?
sections.html:
Wikipedia reports that Russell County has the highest share in the nation of residents who work in another state, over 54%, and that most of them work in Columbus, Georgia.

  • Phenix City unofficially keeps Eastern time even though Alabama is on Central time. The county's own website lists many events with an ET tag.
  • U.S. 80 and U.S. 280 run toward Columbus, and U.S. 431 and several state routes also serve the county.
  • Wikipedia lists the Phenix City Express as local transit.

Where a house sits relative to Phenix City and the Georgia line matters to anyone who commutes, so say so plainly when you describe a property in Hurtsboro or the rural south.

sections.h2: Which communities and schools are in Russell County?
sections.html:
Phenix City is the only city, Hurtsboro is the one town, and Ladonia is a census-designated place. The unincorporated list is long: Cottonton, Crawford, Fort Mitchell, Glenville, Hatchechubbee, Holy Trinity, Hooks, Jernigan, Mahrt, Pittsview, Sandfort, Seale, Uchee and Wende.

Wikipedia lists the Russell County School District for the county. School boundaries follow addresses, so confirm the district for a specific house before you compare properties.

The county's official site points to the Chattahoochee Indian Heritage Center and the Fort Mitchell National Historic Landmark as local attractions. It also describes the Chattahoochee River for kayaking and fishing, and the Eufaula National Wildlife Refuge reaches into the county. A house near the river or refuge is worth checking with an insurer for flood questions.

sections.h2: What did the 2020 census show about Russell County households?
sections.html:
There were 23,997 households in Russell County in 2020, in 27,253 housing units. Of the occupied units, 57.1% were owner-occupied and 42.9% were rented.

The population grew 11.8% between 2010 and 2020, from 52,947 to 59,183, and the 2025 estimate shows a small step back to 58,898. About 40% of the county lives in rural areas, so many properties sit outside city lines.

sections.h2: When are Russell County property taxes due, and when is the tax sale?
sections.html:
Alabama property taxes are due October 1 and turn delinquent after December 31. Under the state calendar, unpaid parcels are sent to probate court in February and advertised in April.

  • October 1: taxes due.
  • January 1: delinquent.
  • February: sent to probate court.
  • April: advertised for sale.
  • May: tax sale.

The Russell County website lists a Revenue Commissioner's delinquent tax sale held May 5, 2026, with registration due by 9:30 am Eastern. It also lists an October 14, 2026 notice from the Revenue Office about property taxes. The county courthouse is at 1000 Broad Street in Phenix City. Check the county site for the current notice before you rely on any date, since mailing and payment details can change from year to year.

sections.h2: Is Russell County planning for growth?
sections.html:
The county has been collecting public input on a long-range plan. Its website carries a September 8, 2026 notice for Russell County Comprehensive Plan 2050 meetings, inviting residents to speak up.

A plan like that can shape zoning, roads and utilities over the coming decades, so owners of land outside Phenix City may want to watch the meetings. The same site also lists a public meeting on pickleball in Fort Mitchell and an alert system for emergencies, signs of a county that is active in its smaller communities.

sections.h2: What homestead exemptions are available to Russell County owners?
sections.html:
A homestead exemption reduces the taxable value of a single-family home you own and occupy as your primary residence on the first day of the tax year, on up to 160 acres. You apply through the county office.

  • Under 65: up to $4,000 of assessed value off the state tax and up to $2,000 off the county tax.
  • Age 65 or older with income at or under $12,000 on the combined federal return: exempt from all ad valorem taxes (type H-3).
  • Permanently and totally disabled: exempt from all ad valorem taxes, with no income limit (also H-3).
  • Age 65 or older with higher income: exempt from the state portion, plus the regular $2,000 county exemption (H-4).

The exemption is tied to the owner. When a house sells, the next owner has to apply.

sections.h2: What does the deed tax cost when a Russell County house sells?
sections.html:
The deed tax is 50 cents per $500 of value, set by Alabama Code 40-22-1, and it is collected when the probate judge's office records the deed. A sale at $150,000 works out to 300 units of $500, so $150 in tax.

The statute requires proof of the real price paid, and it allows the taxable amount to drop by a mortgage on which mortgage tax was already paid. Deeds made for nominal consideration to fix a title defect are excluded. One third of the tax goes to the county treasury and two thirds to the state.

sections.h2: What do Russell County sellers face, and where does a cash sale fit?
sections.html:
Sellers here often own a house inherited from family, a rental with tenants, or a property where repairs have piled up. The Columbus commute market is steady, but older houses still need money to list well.

Cash Home Buyers reviews Russell County houses as they stand, from Phenix City neighborhoods to Seale, Crawford and Hurtsboro, and replies with a written offer. A cash closing can skip appraisals tied to a buyer's loan, and you can ask about timing that fits a tax deadline or a move.

faqs.q: What county is Phenix City, AL in?
faqs.a: Phenix City is in Russell County, Alabama, and it is the county seat. A small part of the city lies in Lee County.

faqs.q: When are Russell County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1. They become delinquent after December 31, and unpaid parcels follow the state schedule toward a May tax sale.

faqs.q: How much is the deed tax in Russell County?
faqs.a: It is 50 cents for each $500 of value conveyed, under Alabama Code 40-22-1. The probate judge's office collects it when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Does Russell County use Eastern or Central time?
faqs.a: Alabama is officially on Central time, but Phenix City unofficially uses Eastern time. The county website lists events with an ET tag.
